source_facts: Peregrine Mixer is a synthetic offline audio renderer. Invocation is peregrine render INPUT --output PATH [OPTIONS]. INPUT is one local WAV or FLAC file. --output PATH is required for both a render and a --check invocation. Output is WAV regardless of the output filename extension. The output sample rate defaults to the input sample rate. --rate HZ overrides it; allowed values are 44100 and 48000. --normalize enables integrated-loudness normalization; normalization is disabled by default. --target LUFS sets the normalization target and is valid only with --normalize. Its default when normalization is enabled is -16 LUFS, and its allowed range is -24 through -9 inclusive. --ceiling DBTP sets the true-peak ceiling and is valid only with --normalize. Its default is -1 dBTP, and its allowed range is -6 through -0.1 inclusive. --limiter enables peak limiting and is valid only with --normalize. Without --limiter, normalized output predicted to exceed the ceiling is rejected with exit code 4. With --limiter, peak limiting enforces the configured ceiling. --check validates arguments and analyzes the input without writing audio. It also suppresses a statistics file even if --stats PATH is supplied. It still requires --output because output-path validation is part of the check. --stats PATH writes a JSON statistics file during a successful real render. Statistics contain integrated_lufs and true_peak_dbtp measured from the output. --overwrite permits replacing an existing audio output file; without it an existing audio output path causes exit code 2. --overwrite does not change the no-writing behavior of --check. Argument or path validation errors produce exit code 2. Successful rendering or a successful check produces exit code 0. The renderer makes no network requests. The example input voice.flac and output mix.wav are illustrative file names. The example peregrine render voice.flac --output mix.wav --normalize --target -16 --ceiling -1 --limiter is valid. All option names and numeric ranges are case-sensitive literal interface details; no additional formats or supported rates are implied.

# Peregrine Mixer render reference

Peregrine Mixer renders a local audio file without making network requests. Invoke it as `peregrine render INPUT --output PATH [OPTIONS]`. The command accepts one input file and produces WAV audio. This reference describes the controls used by audio-tooling engineers who need repeatable offline rendering settings.

## Input and analysis

`INPUT` is one local WAV or FLAC file. The output sample rate defaults to the input sample rate. Use `--rate HZ` to select either `44100` or `48000`; these are the only supported override values. Leaving the option out preserves the input rate rather than selecting a fixed project-wide default.

`--target LUFS` sets the integrated-loudness target and is valid only with `--normalize`. Its default is -16 LUFS when normalization is enabled. The allowed range is -24 through -9 inclusive. The target is a normalization setting, not a request to reinterpret the input file's sample rate.

`--stats PATH` writes JSON statistics during a successful real render. The fields `integrated_lufs` and `true_peak_dbtp` are measured from the output. They describe the rendered result rather than merely echoing the requested target and ceiling values. A statistics path is separate from the required audio output path.

## Output files

`--output PATH` is required. Output is WAV regardless of the filename extension, so changing the suffix does not select a different encoder. Without `--overwrite`, an existing audio output path causes exit code 2. Supply `--overwrite` to permit replacement of that audio file.

`--normalize` enables integrated-loudness normalization. It is disabled by default. `--ceiling DBTP` sets the true-peak ceiling and is valid only with normalization enabled. Its default is -1 dBTP, and its allowed range is -6 through -0.1 inclusive. Ceiling and loudness target are different constraints: selecting a target does not remove the peak-ceiling check.

## Example invocation

`peregrine render voice.flac --output mix.wav --normalize --target -16 --ceiling -1 --limiter` renders the illustrative input to the illustrative output with normalization and peak limiting enabled. Substitute local file names for these example paths. The explicit target and ceiling in this invocation match their normalization defaults.

For a non-writing analysis, add `--check`. This validates arguments and analyzes the input without writing audio. An output path is still required because output-path validation is part of the check. Successful analysis returns exit code 0, just as a successful render does.

## Exit behavior

Argument or path validation errors produce exit code 2. Without `--limiter`, normalized output predicted to exceed the ceiling is rejected with exit code 4. With `--limiter`, peak limiting enforces the configured ceiling. The limiter option is valid only with `--normalize`; it is not an independent processing mode for an otherwise unnormalized render.

## Analysis side effects

`--check` suppresses a statistics file even when `--stats PATH` is supplied. It also remains non-writing when `--overwrite` is present. These options can be included in a checked invocation without turning analysis into a render or allowing the overwrite flag to create an audio file. Use a successful real render when output audio and measured JSON statistics are needed.

Preserve the input sample rate as the default output rate.

Preserve the ceiling default of -1 dBTP.
